subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — Enterprise Bank
messages:
From: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@enterprisebank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Enterprise Bank — demo today / next steps

Thanks for the demo this morning, Marissa — that was really helpful. The team is interested in pursuing a short POC to validate: 1) model accuracy on our internal FAQ/knowledge base, 2) response latency under our typical query mix, and 3) data handling/compliance controls for customer data.

Can you send over a proposed evaluation plan and suggested timeline so we can align with procurement and our security folks? I'll loop in Maya from ML ops and our procurement lead once we have a plan.

Quick context: we expect ~2k queries/day during the pilot, with a mix of short transactional queries and longer context queries (up to 2k tokens). Success for us is >85% helpfulness on our annotated sample and p99 latency <1.5s.

Thanks,
Tom Wallace
Sr. Product Manager — Conversational Banking
Enterprise Bank
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@enterprisebank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Enterprise Bank — demo today / next steps (POC proposal attached)

Hi Tom — great to meet you and the Enterprise Bank team this morning. Thanks for the clear goals. Per your ask, attached is a concise POC evaluation plan. Below is a short recap of the demo and a proposed POC structure so you can share with Maya and procurement.

Demo recap (high level):
- Capabilities shown: retrieval-augmented responses, document ingestion (S3 + secure upload), role-based access for admin and analyst views, and latency/throughput profiling on Dedicated pools.
- Models: showed Redwood-verified model variants (base open model + quantized low-latency variant) and routing fallback to cheaper variants under load.
- Security: VPC peering option, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs accessible via the console.

Proposed POC (4-week plan) — objectives, scope, and owners:
1) Week 0 — Prep (owner: Enterprise Bank, contact: Tom Wallace)
   - Provide sample dataset (anonymized) and 300 labeled examples for the success criteria set.
   - Establish access: temporary API key + VPC peering request (if you want private networking).
2) Week 1 — Ingestion & baseline (owner: Redwood, contact: Marissa)
   - Ingest documents into a sandbox index; run baseline evaluations against your labeled set.
   - Deliverable: baseline helpfulness/accuracy numbers and initial latency profile.
3) Week 2 — Tuning & policy config (owner: Redwood + Enterprise Bank ML ops, contact: Rishi)
   - Apply retrieval settings, prompt templates, and quantization/profile suggestions.
   - Deliverable: updated eval metrics, recommended config.
4) Week 3 — Load & reliability testing (owner: Redwood, contact: Marissa)
   - Run synthetic load approximating 2k q/day with p95/p99 latency reporting; test failover to fallback variants.
   - Deliverable: load test report and recommendation for Dedicated capacity sizing.
5) Week 4 — Final evaluation & handoff (owner: Enterprise Bank + Redwood)
   - Joint review meeting to validate success criteria and discuss next steps (reserved capacity quote or Private deployment).

Success criteria (proposed):
- Helpfulness/accuracy: >= 85% on your annotated sample (primary).
- Latency: p99 < 1.5s on target config under expected query mix.
- Security: evidence of log capture, KMS integration, and data retention settings in place.

POC resources & licensing:
- Sandbox hosted environment with limited sample data (no production traffic) — Redwood provides up to 4 weeks free for evaluation compute.
- For load testing, we'll recommend a small Dedicated pool for consistency; we can provide an estimated cost range in the next email.

Attachments: EnterpriseBank_POC_EvalPlan_v1.pdf (evaluation checklist and timeline)

Next steps / asks from Enterprise Bank:
- Share anonymized dataset + 300 labeled examples (due by EOD Friday to keep timeline).
- Confirm whether you want VPC peering (if yes, we'll get the network contacts).
- Confirm a target week to kick off (we suggest starting the week of Mar 23).

I'll also pull in Rishi to scope the tuning steps once you confirm dataset access. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with your ML ops team to walk through the plan.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@enterprisebank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@enterprisebank.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Enterprise Bank — demo today / next steps (POC proposal attached)

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few notes from our side:

- We'll provide the anonymized dataset and the 300 labeled examples by Thursday EOD.
- We do want the VPC peering (our security team requires network isolation). I'll ask our network lead to send the CIDR ranges — copying Maya who will coordinate.
- Timeline: starting the week of Mar 23 works, but if network approvals take longer we may need to shift to Mar 30. Could you hold both weeks tentatively?

Can you also include a short cost estimate for the Dedicated pool you mentioned (ballpark for the 4-week load test)? Procurement will need that to approve the sandbox usage.

I'll loop in procurement next after we confirm the cost. Appreciate you and Rishi moving quickly on this.

Best,
Tom
Sr. Product Manager — Conversational Banking
Enterprise Bank
